corrections.compiler_and_flags: Dart 3.13 (dart/config.yaml engines aot: /app/server, vm: dart run /app/server.dart); jet_server ^0.2.0 from pub (dart/jet_server/pubspec.yaml). Drogon 1.9.13: cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=release (CMake release flags), C++17, no LTO; no C++ compiler version pinned in the suite files read (cpp/drogon/config.yaml language version '14/17'); config.json threads_num 0 (auto), log level WARN, Server and Date headers disabled. No server_cpu_cores or server_cpu_saturation metric is recorded for any Dart row.
corrections.caveats: The suite entry dart/jet_server/server.dart was written by the jet_server author (suite commits b869a75, ac9f6f2 and b3f17f2 by Wdestroier) and is specialised to the benchmark: it returns pre-built response byte arrays, routes by comparing raw bytes, sends no Content-Type header and uses no router, while the Drogon entry runs Drogon's routing (a sync advice for GET /, UserCtrl for the /user routes) and builds HttpResponse objects with Content-Type: text/plain; jet_server averages 62.3 bytes received per request vs 78.3 for Drogon (derived from total_bytes_received / total_requests), so handler work is not equal. The library is pure Dart: lib/src holds buffer_pool, constants, http_parser, jet_server_impl and syscall .dart files and the package depends only on ffi, so the event loop and parser are Dart code calling libc epoll/read/write through dart:ffi; the near-equal AOT and VM rows mean the JIT reaches AOT speed after warmup or both rows hit a common ceiling, not that a native C loop does the work. No Dart row in data.json (jet_server, shelf, relic, spry) carries the suite's server_cpu_saturation / server_cpu_cores validity probe, so whether jet_server was server-bound, or ran under the same 4-CPU allotment as Drogon, cannot be checked. The top rows at 256 connections cluster within 1.5% (morojs-engine 259,617, morojs 259,418, jet_server-vm 256,385, caprese 256,004, jet_server 255,549), consistent with a shared ceiling. The README prints no numbers and points to the-benchmarker; its own benchmarks/jet_vs_shelf compares only against Dart's shelf. The project calls itself experimental and targets Linux/WSL only; 8 commits, 1 star. Suite-level weaknesses: published snapshots move a lot between runs (Drogon 101,282-179,279 req/s across the 2026-09-15 to 2026-10-06 snapshots) and a snapshot gives no repeat spread; the suite README says a run is server-bound only above 75% CPU saturation and invalid below 50%, and in the 2026-10-06 snapshot the 60 fastest rows sit at 49-63% (Drogon 62-63%), so the ceiling for the fastest servers may be the load generator or the box rather than the server; the presence of the server_cpu_saturation / server_cpu_cores probe places this snapshot in the README's current zrk --closed keep-alive revision, although the README's contract paragraph still describes oha with keep-alive disabled; the workload is three trivial routes (GET /, GET /user/:id, POST /user) with near-empty bodies. The C/C++ rows are only Drogon 1.9.13 (cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=release, threads_num 0 = auto, Server and Date headers disabled, no LTO), oatpp 1.3, agoo-c 0.7 and cwist 3.9 (C); cwist is the best C row at 64 connections (186,252) and agoo-c at 256 and 512; nginx, h2o and lithium are not rows in this suite. Same table, losers to Drogon at 256 connections: Crystal toro 166,910, Go fasthttp 166,243, C# aspnet-minimal-api 147,805 vs Drogon 178,341. The CPU string 'M1 Eight-Core Processor' on an x86_64 Fedora kernel is not a recognisable CPU model, and no C++ compiler version is pinned in the suite files read (cpp/drogon/config.yaml language version '14/17'), which is why this is B and not A.
corrections.why_faster: Event loop, HTTP parser and buffer pool written in Dart over libc epoll/read/write via dart:ffi (lib/src/syscall.dart; no native code), one isolate per reported CPU with SO_REUSEPORT; the suite handler returns pre-built response bytes with byte-compare routing and no Content-Type header, so it does less per-request work than Drogon's router and HttpResponse path. The margin is not explained by the project.

notes: Numbers verified in data.json (2026-10-06) and repeated in the 2026-10-02 snapshot; kept at B like the earlier the-benchmarker entries (caprese, morojs, hyper). Shortcomings to record: first-party benchmark-specialised suite entry (pre-built responses, no router, no Content-Type), no saturation probe for any Dart row, top rows clustered at a possible shared ceiling, 1-star experimental project; the record's 'native epoll loop' inference was wrong (the loop is Dart over dart:ffi).
